idiom_name: function-pointer seam plus hand-written expectation check
implementation_notes: C has no reflection and no virtual dispatch, so the mock is hand-built: the collaborator's role becomes a struct of function pointers (or a link-time seam that replaces the real symbols for the test binary), and each mock function compares the arguments it receives with the programmed expectation and fails the test immediately. Nothing in the language replaces the classic structure - cmocka ships mock facilities and CMock generates expectation-checking mocks from headers, but neither is dominant enough to be the default - so the hand-written seam remains the baseline. The SUT must receive the function table through a parameter or context struct; the classic form stays justified when the seam already exists and only one or two interactions are verified.
pitfalls: Expectation-checking functions must repeat the real signature and the compiler cannot check it across translation units, so a drifted parameter list links silently and fails at runtime.
Link seams (--wrap, weak symbols, macro replacement of the real name) bypass the type system and can leave part of the binary still talking to the real implementation.
File-scope counters and expectation state are shared by the whole test binary; reset them in setup or keep the expectation state in a struct the test allocates per case.
